spans.s:
सीदत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, sinking, desponding, pining,
grieving, sorrowing; decaying, perishing; distressed,
pained; going.

सीदत् सीदत्, सीदमान. See under rt.
1. सद्, p. 1055, col. 2.
सीदमान, अस्, आ, अम्, sinking down, &c.

सिद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, accomplished, effected, com-
pleted, finished, perfected, fulfilled, performed, ob-
tained, acquired, gained; succeeded, successful;
settled, established, substantiated, demonstrated,
proved; valid (as a rule of grammar or in law);
admitted to be true or right; adjudicated, decided,
terminated (as a lawsuit); paid, liquidated, settled
(as a debt); ready (as money); thoroughly pre-
pared, concocted, compounded (as drugs &c.);
cooked, dressed; matured, ripened, ripe; subjugated,
subdued, brought into subjection (by magical power);
thoroughly skilled or versed (in magical arts &c.);
perfected or sanctified (by penance, austerities, &c.);
emancipated, beatified; endowed with supernatural
powers or faculties, (of these eight are usually enu-
merated, see under सिद्धि below; but twenty-six
others are sometimes added, e. g. दूर-श्रवण,
सर्वज्ञ-त्व, मनोयायि-त्व, वह्नि-स्तम्भ, &c.,
see under स्तम्भ); sacred, holy, pious, divine,
immortal, eternal; well-known, eminent, celebrated;
illustrious, shining, splendid; (अस्), m. a semi-divine
being supposed to be of great purity and holiness,
and said to be specially characterized by the eight
supernatural faculties (of which अणिमन् is the first;
see under सिद्धि; according to some the Siddhas
inhabit, together with the Munis &c., the Bhuvar-
loka or middle region between the earth and the
sun; according to the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa eighty-eight
thousand of them occupy the regions of the sky
north of the sun and south of the seven Ṛṣis;
they are regarded as immortal, but only in the sense
of living to the end of a Kalpa; in the later mytho-
logy they appear to be sometimes confused with the
Sādhyas, whose place they seem occasionally to take,
see साध्य); an inspired sage or seer (as Vyāsa and
others); any holy or sanctified personage or great
saint (especially one who by austere practices has
attained some or all of the five states of beatitude,
see सलोक-ता, सरूप-ता, सामीप्य, सायुज्य,
सार्ष्टि-ता); an adept in magical or mystical arts,
one who by the performance of certain mystical rites
has acquired superhuman powers, (see above and
under सिद्धि); a lawsuit, judicial trial (= व्यव-
हार); a kind of dark Dhustūra or thorn-apple;
another plant or a sort of hard sugar (= गुड); N.
of the twenty-first of the astronomical Yogas; (आस्),
m. pl., N. of a people; (आ), f. a medicinal plant or
root (= ऋद्धि); N. of one of the eight Yoginīs,
(see under योगिन्); (अम्), n. sea-salt.
—सिद्ध-
कामेश्वरी, f. one of the five forms of Kāmākhyā
or Durgā.
—सिद्ध-केरल, अम्, n. ‘the perfect
Kerala,’ N. of a district.
—सिद्ध-क्षेत्र, अम्, n.,
N. of a place.
—सिद्ध-गङ्गा, f. the divine or
heavenly Ganges (= मन्दाकिनी).
—सिद्ध-ग्रह,
अस्, m., N. of a particular kind of madness or seizure
(produced by supernatural agency).
—सिद्ध-जल,
अम्, n. ‘cooked water,’ the fermented water of
boiled rice or sour rice-gruel.
—सिद्ध-ता, f. or
सिद्ध-त्व, अम्, n. perfection, completion; the
establishment or validity of a rule or doctrine.
—सिद्ध-देव, अस्, m. ‘perfected deity,’ epithet
of Śiva.
—सिद्ध-धातु, उस्, m. ‘perfected mineral,’
[]
quicksilver.
—सिद्ध-धामन्, अ, n. the abode of
the Siddhas.
—सिद्ध-पक्ष, अस्, m. the established
or logical side of an argument.
—सिद्ध-पीठ, अस्,
m. a most sacred station or shrine; a place sacred
to Durgā.
—सिद्ध-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a mythical
city said to be located in the southern or lower
regions of the earth.
—सिद्ध-पुरुष, अस्, m. a
perfect or completely sanctified personage; a sage, seer;
an adept in mystical rites.
—सिद्ध-पुष्प, अस्, m.
‘having perfect flowers,’ the Kara-vīra plant.
—सिद्-
ध-प्रयोजन, अस्, m. white mustard.
—सिद्ध-
प्राय, अस्, आ, अम्, almost accomplished, nearly com-
pleted, almost finished.
—सिद्ध-भूमि, इस्, f. the
region inhabited by Siddhas.
—सिद्ध-मनोरम,
अस्, m., N. of the second day of the civil month
(कर्म-मास).
—सिद्ध-मन्त्र, अस्, m. a parti-
cular Mantra of great efficacy.
—सिद्ध-मोदक,
अस्, m. a particular kind of candied sugar prepared
from the Tavarāja plant.
—सिद्ध-यात्रिक, अस्, m.
a pilgrim who seeks the region of the Siddhas.
—सिद्ध-योगिन्, ई, m. epithet of Śiva; (इनी), f.,
N. of a particular Yoginī; of the goddess Manasā.
—सिद्ध-योगेश्वर-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a
Tantra work.
—सिद्ध-रस, अस्, आ, अम्, having
perfected metallic fluids, mineral, metallic; (अस्), m.
‘perfected mineral,’ quicksilver; skilled in the science
of metals, an alchemist.
—सिद्ध-रुद्रेश्वर-तीर्थ
(˚र-ईश्˚), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—सिद्ध-वट,
N. of a place.
—सिद्ध-वटी, f., N. of a tutelary
goddess.
—सिद्ध-विद्या, f. the worship of Durgā
under a particular form.
—सिद्ध-सङ्कल्प, अस्, आ,
अम्, one who has accomplished his wishes.
—सिद्-
ध-सङ्घ, अस्, m. a company of Siddhas, assem-
blage of saints.
—सिद्ध-सलिल, अम्, n. ‘cooked
water,’ sour rice-gruel.
—सिद्ध-साधक, अस्, m.
epithet of Śiva.
—सिद्ध-साधन, अस्, m. white
mustard; (अम्), n. the performance of magical or
mystical rites (for the acquisition of supernatural
powers, &c.); the materials employed in mystical
or chemical processes.
—सिद्ध-साधन-दोष,
अस्, m. the error of labouring to establish what is
already proved.
—सिद्ध-साध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, who
or what has effected what was to be done; effected,
accomplished, proved; (अस्), m. a particular Mantra;
(अम्), n. demonstrated proof or conclusion.
—सिद्-
ध-सारस्वत, N. of a work.
—सिद्धसारस्वत-
दीपिका, f., N. of a commentary by Padmanābha on
the Bhuvaneśvarī-stotra.
—सिद्ध-सिद्ध, अस्, m. a
particular Mantra.
—सिद्ध-सिन्धु, उस्, f. ‘divine
river,’ epithet of the Ganges.
—सिद्ध-सुसिद्ध,
अस्, m. a particular Mantra.
—सिद्ध-सेन, अस्, m.
‘having a divine or perfect army,’ epithet of Kārtti-
keya (god of war); of an astronomer.
—सिद्ध-
सेन-दिवाकर, अस्, m., N. of a son of Sarva-jña
and pupil of Vṛddha-vāda-sūri (said to have induced
Vikramāditya to tolerate the Jaina religion).
—सिद्-
ध-सेवित, अस्, आ, अम्, honoured or worshipped
by Siddhas; (अस्), m. epithet of a form of Bhairava
or Śiva (= वटुक-भैरव).
—सिद्ध-स्थाली,
f. the boiler or pot of a seer (fabled as a vessel
bestowed by a holy personage, and gifted with the
property of overflowing with any kind of food at
the wish of the possessor).
—सिद्धान्त (˚ध-
अन्˚), अस्, m. established end [cf. राद्धान्त];
demonstrated conclusion of an argument, the esta-
blished line of reasoning or view of any question,
the true logical conclusion (following on the refuta-
tion of the पूर्व-पक्ष or first objection), esta-
blished truth, proved fact, settled opinion or doc-
trine, dogma, axiom, received or admitted truth
(regarded as of four kinds, viz. सर्व-तन्त्र-स्˚,
प्रति-तन्त्र-स्˚, अधिकरण-स्˚, अभ्युपगम-
स्˚, q. q. v. v.); any fixed or established text-book
resting on conclusive arguments, (often used at the
end of comps. to denote certain received treatises
by high authorities on astronomy, mathematics, and
other sciences; nine astronomical works being espe-
cially so designated, viz. the Brahma-s˚, Sūrya-s˚,
Soma-s˚, Vṛhaspati-s˚, Garaga-s˚, Nārada-s˚, Parā-
śara-s˚, Pulastya-s˚, Vasiṣṭha-s˚; five principal astro-
nomical Siddhāntas are enumerated by others, viz.
[]
Pauliśa-s˚, Romaka-s˚, Vāsiṣṭha-s˚, Śaura-s˚, and
Paitāmaha-s˚.)
—सिद्धान्त-कोटि, इस्, f. the point in
an argument which is regarded as a logical conclu-
sion.
—सिद्धान्त-कौमुदी, f., N. of a celebrated
grammar by Bhaṭṭoji-dīkṣita (intended to furnish
a practical arrangement of Pāṇini's Sūtras with a
commentary).
—सिद्धान्त-गर्भ, अस्, m., N. of
a work by Madana-pāla.
—सिद्धान्त-चन्द्रिका,
f. a commentary on the Sarasvatī-sūtra by Rāma-
candrāśrama; another on the Śāstra-dīpikā by
Rāma-kṛṣṇa-bhaṭṭa; N. of Rāma-saṃyamin's Ve-
dānta precepts.
—सिद्धान्तचन्द्रिका-टीका, f. a
commentary by Gaṅgādhara-yati on Rāma-saṃya-
min's work.
—सिद्धान्त-चन्द्रोदय (˚र-उद्˚),
अस्, m. a commentary by Kṛṣṇa-dhūrjaṭi-dīkṣita
on the Tarka-saṅgraha.
—सिद्धान्त-चिन्तामणि,
इस्, m., N. of a work on astronomy.
—सिद्धान्त-
तत्त्व, अम्, n., N. of a work on the principles of
the Vaiśeṣika doctrines, (also called Padārtha-viveka.)
—सिद्धान्ततत्त्व-बिन्दु, a commentary by Ma-
dhu-sūdana-sarasvatī on Śaṅkarācārya's Daśa-ślokī.
—सिद्धान्ततत्त्वबिन्दु-सन्दीपन or बिन्दु-
सन्दीपन, अम्, n. a commentary by Puruṣottama
Sarasvatī on the preceding.
—सिद्धान्ततत्त्व-सर्-
वस्व, अम्, n. a commentary on the Siddhānta-
tattva by Gopīnātha-maunin.
—सिद्धान्त-दीपिका,
f. a commentary on the Siddhānta-muktāvalī by
Nānā-dīkṣita.
—सिद्धान्त-पक्ष, अस्, m. the
logically correct side of an argument.
—सिद्धान्त-
बिन्दु = सिद्धान्ततत्त्व-बिन्दु, q. v.
—सिद्धान्-
तबिन्दु-व्याख्या, f. a commentary by Nārāyaṇa-
yati on the preceding.
—सिद्धान्त-मुक्तावली, f.
‘string of pearls of dogmatic precepts,’ N. of a com-
mentary by Viśva-nātha Pañcānana Bhaṭṭācārya
Tarkālaṅkāra on the Bhāṣā-pariccheda (a text-
book of the Nyāya, also called मुक्तावली); of a
metrical Vedānta treatise with a prose interpretation
by Prakāśānanda; of a metrical exposition of the
theory of Vallabhācārya.
—सिद्धान्तमुक्तावली-
प्रकाश, अस्, m., N. of a commentary on the Sid-
dhānta-muktāvalī.
—सिद्धान्त-रत्न, N. of a
summary of the Vedānta system by Nimbārka (=
दश-श्लोकी).
—सिद्धान्त-रहस्य, अम्, n., N. of
a work on astronomy.
—सिद्धान्त-लेश, अस्, m.,
N. of a metrical work by Apya-dīkṣita on the
Vedānta and other systems of philosophy.
—सिद्-
धान्त-वागीश, अस्, m., N. of the preceptor of
Rāghavendra.
—सिद्धान्त-शिरोमणि, N. of an
astronomical work by Bhāskara.
—सिद्धान्त-सङ्-
ग्रह, अस्, m., N. of an epitome of Vijñāneśvara's
Mitākṣarā.
—सिद्धान्त-सन्दर्भ, अस्, m., N.
of an astronomical work.
—सिद्धान्त-सुन्दर,
N. of a work on astronomy by Jñāna-rāja.
—सिद्-
धान्त-सूक्ति-मञ्जरी, f., N. of a metrical abridg-
ment of the Siddhānta-leśa by Gaṅgā-dhara-sarasvatī.
—सिद्धान्ताचार (˚त-आच्˚), अस्, m. a perfect rule
of action (with the Tāntrikas); one who practises
this rule (said to consist in purity, quietism, and
complete mental absorption in Durgā).
—सिद्धान्-
तित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. सिद्धान्त), logically demon-
strated or proved, established as true.
—सिद्धान्तिन्,
ई, m. one who establishes or proves his conclusions;
one learned in scientific text-books; a follower of
the Mīmāṃsā philosophy.
—सिद्धान्न (˚ध-अन्˚),
अम्, n. dressed food, cooked victuals.
—सिद्धापगा
(˚ध-अप्˚), f. ‘divine river,’ epithet of the Ganges.
—सिद्धारि (˚ध-अरि), इस्, m. a particular Mantra.
—सिद्धार्थ (˚ध-अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, one who has
accomplished an aim or object, successful, prosperous;
(अस्), m. epithet of the great Buddha (or Śākya-
muni, founder of the Buddhist religion); N. of the
father of the last and most celebrated Arhat of the
present Ava-sarpiṇī; epithet of Śiva; white mustard;
(आ), f., N. of the mother of the fourth of the
twenty-four Arhats.
—सिद्धार्थक, अम्, n. white
mustard.
—सिद्धार्थ-कारिन्, ई, m. epithet of Śiva.
—सिद्धार्थिन् (˚ध-अर्˚), ई, m., N. of the fifty-
third (or twenty-seventh) year of Jupiter's cycle of
sixty years.
—सिद्धाश्रम (˚ध-आश्˚), N. of a
hermitage in the Himālaya (where Viṣṇu performed
penance before his dwarf incarnation).
—सिद्धा-
[]
श्रम-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—सिद्धा-
सन (˚ध-आस्˚), अम्, n. a particular posture in
religious meditation (described as placing the left
heel under the body and the right heel in front of
it, fixing the sight between the eyebrows, and medi-
tating upon the syllable ॐ).
—सिद्धेश्वर-तन्त्र
(˚ध-ईश्˚), अम्, n., N. of a Tantra work.
—सिद्-
धेश्वर-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—सिद्-
धेश्वरी (˚ध-ईश्˚), f., N. of a particular goddess.
—सिद्धौघ (˚ध-ओघ), अस्, m., N. of a par-
ticular class of Gurus worshipped or revered by the
Tāntrikas, (their names are said to be Nārada,
Kāśyapa, Śambhu, Bhārgava, Kula-kauśika.)
सिद्धा. See under सिद्ध, p. 1114, col. 2.

सिद्धिली सिद्धिली, f. (according to some)
a small ant.

सिद्धक, अस्, m. a kind of tree (= सिन्धु-
वार); the Śāl tree; a species of metre.

सिद्धायिका, f., N. of one of the twenty-four
goddesses, called Śāsana-devatās, who execute the
commands of the twenty-four Arhats.

सिद्धि, इस्, f. accomplishment, fulfilment, com-
pletion, perfection, complete attainment (of any
object), performance; success, prosperity, well-being;
settlement, establishment, substantiation, demonstra-
tion, proof, indisputable conclusion; validity (of a
rule or law); certainty, truth, accuracy, correctness;
decision, adjudication, determination (of a lawsuit);
payment, liquidation (of a debt), acquittance; the
solution of a problem; preparation, cooking, matur-
ing, maturity; readiness; complete knowledge;
complete perfection or sanctification (by penance
&c.); final emancipation, supreme felicity, beati-
tude; the acquisition of supernatural powers by
magical means or the supernatural faculty so ac-
quired, (eight are usually enumerated, e. g. अणिमन्,
महिमन्, लघिमन्, गरिमन्, प्राप्ति, प्रा-
काम्य, ईशि-त्व, वशि-त्व, q. q. v. v., to which is
sometimes added कामावसायि-त्व and many others,
e. g. सिद्धिः खेचरी, the magical power of flying
through the air; रसोल्लास, q. v., वि-शोका, q. v., see
also under सिद्ध, p. 1114); any marvellous skill or
capability; a magical shoe or slipper (supposed to
have the power of conveying the wearer wherever
he likes); good effect or result, use, advantage; un-
derstanding, intellect; concealment, vanishing, mak-
ing one's self invisible; a particular Yoga (either the
sixteenth of the astronomical periods or the nine-
teenth of the twenty-eight astrological Yogas); a
kind of medicinal root (= ऋद्धि); Perfection (per-
sonified as a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of
Dharma); N. of a Yoginī; of Durgā; of Śiva, (in
this sense masc.)
—सिद्धि-कारण, अम्, n. a cause
of beatitude, means of obtaining felicity.
—सिद्धि-
चामुण्डा-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—सिद्धि-
द, अस्, आ, अम्, conferring felicity or beatitude; (अस्),
m. epithet of a form of Bhairava or Śiva (= वटुक-
भैरव).
—सिद्धि-दात्री, f. ‘giver of perfection,’
epithet of Durgā.
—सिद्धि-भैरव, अम्, n., N.
of a Tantra work.
—सिद्धि-योग, अस्, m. a parti-
cular auspicious conjunction of the planets.
—सिद्-
धि-योगिनी, f. a kind of Yoginī.
—सिद्धि-लाभ,
अस्, m. acquirement of success or perfection.
—सिद्-
धि-सोपान, ‘ladder of success,’ N. of a work.
—सिद्धि-स्थान, अम्, n. ‘place of felicity,’ N. of
any sacred spot where final beatitude is obtained by
religious worship (such as particular places on the
Ganges or Sarasvatī).
—सिद्ध्य्-अर्थम्, ind. for
the sake of accomplishing or obtaining.

सिद्ध्वा, ind. having accomplished or effected,
having completed.
सीद्य, अम्, n. slothfulness, idleness, indolence.
